name: DISA STIG, SSH server (RHEL 8)
edition: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 STIG Benchmark v2.0.0
reference: CIS Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 STIG Benchmark v2.0.0, the three rules with Profile Applicability 'STIG': 5.1.28 (MACs employing FIPS 140-2-approved algorithms), 5.1.29 (ciphers employing FIPS 140-2-approved algorithms) and 5.1.30 (FIPS-validated key exchange algorithms). Each sets a CRYPTO_POLICY override with an exact list and fails a server that offers anything else, so this profile is an allowlist of those three lists.
summary: The US Department of Defense hardening for SSH on RHEL 8, from the STIG-only rules of the benchmark: a FIPS 140-2 allowlist of ciphers, MACs and key exchange. Broader than the RHEL 9 STIG (it keeps the AES-CTR ciphers and pins a key-exchange list) but still an allowlist: anything not named fails.
notes: The same CIS RHEL 8 Benchmark carries two different kinds of SSH crypto rule, and this profile encodes only one of them. The Level 1/Level 2 rules (5.1.7 Ciphers, 5.1.16 MACs, ...) are the ordinary CIS denylist, already encoded by cis-benchmark-ssh. The rules with Profile Applicability 'STIG' -- 5.1.28/29/30 -- are different: they are allowlists that name the FIPS 140-2 set exactly and reject the rest, and they are what this profile encodes. The lists are taken verbatim from the CRYPTO_POLICY overrides those rules mandate: Ciphers aes256-ctr,aes192-ctr,aes128-ctr,aes256-gcm@openssh.com,aes128-gcm@openssh.com; MACs hmac-sha2-512,hmac-sha2-256 and their EtM forms; KexAlgorithms the three NIST ECDH curves plus group-exchange-sha256 and the SHA-2 MODP groups 14/16/18. There is no STIG rule for host-key algorithms, so this profile states none (as disa-stig-rhel-9-ssh does). Note the platform difference this documents: the RHEL 8 STIG keeps the AES-CTR ciphers and aes192-ctr and pins an explicit key-exchange list, where the RHEL 9 STIG names only four GCM/CTR ciphers and leaves key exchange to the system crypto-policy; and neither resembles the macOS STIG's single-cipher P-256 set. DISA STIG SSH crypto is per-platform, which is why these are separate profiles rather than editions of one.

cipher.reason: Rule 5.1.29's CRYPTO_POLICY override names exactly these five ciphers.

kex.reason: Rule 5.1.30's CRYPTO_POLICY override names exactly these seven FIPS-validated key exchange methods.

mac.reason: Rule 5.1.28's CRYPTO_POLICY override names hmac-sha2-512 and hmac-sha2-256 in their plain and EtM forms.
